Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Global Assurance Holdings Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Assurance Holdings Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; and Johnathan Hale, Chief Underwriting Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Rivera.

Mike Rivera: Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Global Assurance Holdings Inc.'s performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by robust gross written premiums growth across our lines of business, industry-leading policy retention rates, consistent dividend increases that underscore our commitment to shareholders, and reliable reinsurance recoveries that bolstered our underwriting margins.

Sarah, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Mike. Good morning, everyone. As Mike mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $478 million, or $1.95 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included double-digit top-line expansion, enhanced customer loyalty metrics, progressive shareholder returns, and favorable reinsurance inflows. Our combined ratio was 92.4%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with book value per share at $82.50 and a solvency ratio exceeding 220%.

Let me start by diving into our gross written premiums—or GWP—performance, which came in at $15.8 billion for the quarter, reflecting a robust 12.4% year-over-year growth on a reported basis, or 11.8% on a constant foreign exchange basis. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit GWP expansion, driven by disciplined pricing, industry-leading retention rates averaging 89.2%, and selective new business growth amid a still-hardening P&C market. Excluding the impacts of our mid-year 2022 acquisition of Midwest Specialty Risk—which added about 150 basis points to our top-line growth—we delivered organic GWP growth of 10.2%, underscoring the strength of our core underwriting franchise.

Let me break this down by line of business, where we saw balanced contributions across our portfolio. Starting with Personal Lines, which represent 42% of total GWP, we grew 9.7% to $6.6 billion. Personal Auto was the standout here, up 8.2%—split roughly 5.1% from rate increases, averaging 6.8% achieved through our proprietary GLMs, generalized linear models, and telematics data from our SafeDrive app, now with over 4.2 million enrolled policyholders—and 3.1% from volume, fueled by a 12% uptick in new policies from our direct-to-consumer digital channels. Homeowners and Dwelling Fire premiums surged 14.3% to $3.1 billion, reflecting 9% rate adequacy gains amid persistent rebuild cost inflation, up 7.2% year-over-year per CoreLogic indices, and increased insured values post-2022's Hurricane Ian and California wildfires. Retention held steady at 91%, bolstered by our bundling initiatives, where 68% of new auto policies were written alongside homeowners, mirroring strategies we've seen from peers like Progressive and State Farm.

Shifting to Commercial Lines, 38% of our GWP mix, we posted 13.1% growth to $6.0 billion. Commercial Property led with 16.8% expansion, driven by 11% earned rate increases in a market where capacity remains tight following $50 billion in industry cat losses last year, per Swiss Re sigma estimates. Our focus on preferred risks—limiting exposure to high-hazard coastal zones—enabled us to capture 7% volume growth, including a $250 million book transfer from a softening competitor in the Southeast. Workers' Compensation grew 10.4%, benefiting from 4.2% rate-on-rate improvements via our AI-powered Experience Modification Rating, EMR, analytics, which reduced adverse selection by 15% year-over-year, while General Liability and Umbrella lines advanced 11.2% on strong middle-market demand. Here, our combined retention of 87% reflects proactive account rounding, with 25% of renewals adding cyber endorsements amid rising ransomware threats—echoing the 30% premium hike in D&O lines we've observed industry-wide.

Finally, our Specialty and Global Markets segment, which is 20% of GWP at $3.2 billion, delivered the fastest growth at 17.6%, propelled by 12% rate momentum and 5.6% volume. Cyber insurance premiums jumped 28% to $850 million, capitalizing on the hardening market post-2022's Conti and LockBit surges, where we maintained a sub-60% loss ratio through rigorous third-party vendor vetting and parametric triggers. Marine and Energy lines grew 14%, supported by our Lloyd's syndicate expansion, while Aviation held firm at 9% amid supply chain normalization. This segment's outperformance aligns with our strategy to lean into high-margin, data-rich classes, much like AIG's pivot under their Chartis rebrand.

Regionally, North America drove 65% of our GWP growth, with U.S. P&C rates up 8.5% per our Verisk analytics, outpacing Europe where we saw more modest 6.2% expansion due to softening commercial rates in the UK post-Brexit FCA pricing reforms. Asia-Pacific contributed 9% organic growth, led by our India joint venture with ICICI Lombard, where motor premiums rose 18% on regulatory rate freedom and UBI adoption.

Strategically, these results reflect our three-pillar approach: first, pricing excellence via machine learning models that now price 95% of our book in real-time, delivering 200 basis points of margin accretion; second, distribution innovation, including embedded insurance partnerships with e-commerce platforms akin to Lemonade's model, generating $400 million in new GWP; and third, reinsurance optimization—our 1/1 renewal in January secured $10 billion in cat cover at flat-to-down rates, preserving 85% quota share retention. Looking ahead, we expect FY24 GWP growth of 11-13%, with Personal Lines moderating to 8-10% as auto repair inflation peaks, while Specialty accelerates to 18-20%. This positions us to deliver attritional combined ratio improvement to 94% by year-end.

Before we move on, I'd like to dive deeper into one of our key profitability levers: policy retention rates by major product line. As you know, retention is the lifeblood of our book of business, directly impacting our lifetime value per policyholder, reducing acquisition costs, and stabilizing earned premium growth amid the volatile cycles we've seen in P&C markets.

In Q3, we delivered sequential and year-over-year improvements across the board, achieving a company-wide retention rate of 89.2%, up 140 basis points from Q3 2023 and 80 basis points from Q2 2024. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of retention expansion, driven by disciplined pricing, enhanced customer engagement via our digital ecosystem, and proactive loss ratio management. Lapse rates—our inverse metric—fell to 10.8%, the lowest in five years, reflecting the stickiness of our multi-year policies and bundling strategies.

Let me break this down by our four major product lines: Personal Lines, Auto and Homeowners; Commercial P&C; Life & Annuities; and Group Health & Benefits. I'll highlight the percentages, trends, regional nuances, and the technical initiatives fueling these results.

Personal Lines remains our highest-volume segment, representing 42% of in-force policies and 38% of net written premiums. Retention: 87.5%, up 210 basis points year-over-year. Auto retention hit 88.1%, benefiting from our Snapshot telematics program—similar to Progressive's usage-based model but enhanced with AI-driven behavioral scoring. We've seen a 15% uplift in retention for Snapshot enrollees, as policyholders value the average 12% premium discounts tied to safe driving. Homeowners retention stood at 86.9%, pressured slightly by catastrophe claims in Florida and California but offset by our fortified roof reimbursement program, which reduced non-renews by 8% in high-risk zones.

Regionally, U.S. Southeast retention was 85.2% due to Hurricane Idalia residuals, while Midwest markets exceeded 90% thanks to aggressive bundling—65% of our auto-home bundles renewed at 95%+ rates. Internationally, our UK personal motor book retained at 89.4%, ahead of Aviva's reported 87%, supported by FCA-compliant pricing transparency.

Commercial P&C—Retention: 91.3%, up 110 basis points year-over-year. This segment, 35% of our premium base, continues to outperform on account of mid-market focus and data-rich underwriting. Overall retention reflects strong renewal book quality, with combined ratios holding at 92.4%. Property retention was 92.1%, bolstered by our climate-resilient modeling using RMS and AIR Worldwide catastrophe platforms, which allowed us to price 5-7% above loss trends in wildfire-exposed California. Workers' Comp retention reached 90.8%, up from industry averages around 88% per AM Best data, driven by our EMR optimization tools that helped clients shave 10-15% off premiums.

Regionally, Northeast commercial lines retained at 93.2% amid stable construction activity, while Asia-Pacific markets like Australia dipped to 88.7% due to flood events—though our parametric trigger products there improved renewal loyalty by 12%. Compared to peers like Chubb, our mid-market retention edge stems from API integrations with broker platforms like Verisk IntelliSite.

Life & Annuities—Retention: 94.7%, up 70 basis points year-over-year. Our sticky Life book, 15% of premiums, saw term life retention at 95.2% and whole life/universal life at 94.1%. Annuity persistency—a proxy for retention—held at 96.8% post-surrender, outperforming LIMRA industry benchmarks of 93-94%. This resilience held despite rising interest rates, as our indexed universal life products with guaranteed minimums captured 20% more rollovers from competitors like Prudential.

U.S. retention led at 95.5%, with Europe at 93.2% navigating Solvency II capital charges. Our digital servicing portal, launched last year, reduced lapses by 22% through automated premium reminders and needs-based reviews—akin to Northwestern Mutual's advisor tech but scaled for direct-to-consumer.

Group Health & Benefits—Retention: 92.1%, flat year-over-year, up 50 basis points quarter-over-quarter. Rounding out at 8% of premiums, group health retention stabilized post-ACA Marketplace turbulence. Employer-sponsored plans renewed at 93.4%, with voluntary benefits like dental and vision at 90.2%. We mitigated churn from cost-conscious SMBs via our wellness incentives, mirroring UnitedHealth's Optum model, which boosted participation 18% and retention 9%.

Regionally, U.S. retention was 92.8%, while our Canadian expansion hit 89.5% amid provincial rate filings. Medical loss ratios compressed to 84.2%, supporting premium stability.

These gains aren't accidental. Our 'Retention 95' initiative—targeting 95% company-wide by 2026—leverages three pillars: first, AI-powered personalization; our EagleEye platform analyzes 1.2 petabytes of telematics, claims, and third-party data like LexisNexis Drive to predict churn 90 days out, intervening with tailored offers—yielding a 4.2% retention lift. Second, embedded insurance partnerships: collaborations with auto OEMs like Ford for usage-based auto and homebuilders for parametric home coverage have embedded us in 25% of renewals. Third, pricing discipline: amid softening P&C rates, down 2.1% per Carrier Management indices, we've held flat-to-up 3% renewals, preserving margins without alienating customers.

Looking forward, we guide to 90%+ company-wide retention for FY2024, with upside from our Q4 myAssure app rollout—projecting 2-3% incremental lift via one-click renewals and ARPU-boosting cross-sells. Cat exposure remains monitored, but our $1.8 billion reinsurance tower provides buffer. This positions us for organic growth of 5-7% in earned premiums, outpacing the 3-4% industry consensus.

Turning now to our dividend policy, which remains a cornerstone of our shareholder value creation strategy here at Global Assurance Holdings. As you know, we’ve built a reputation for consistent, growing dividends backed by disciplined underwriting and a fortress balance sheet, much like our peers at Travelers and Chubb. Let me walk you through the details on our dividend payments in USD per share for the quarter and full year, with some forward-looking color.

Starting with the headline: For Q3 2024, our Board approved a quarterly dividend of $0.68 per share, payable on November 15th to shareholders of record as of October 22nd. This marks a 4.6% increase from the $0.65 paid in Q3 2023, reflecting our confidence in sustained earnings power despite a volatile catastrophe year. On a full-year basis, this brings our 2024 total dividend to $2.72 per share, up 5.3% from $2.58 in 2023 and representing our 28th consecutive year of dividend growth. Over the past decade, we’ve delivered a robust 6.2% compound annual growth rate, CAGR, on dividends, outpacing the S&P 500 Insurance Index average of 4.8% and compounding to a total shareholder return of over 220% including reinvested dividends.

Now, let’s drill into the sustainability. Our dividend payout ratio for 2024 stood at 48% of adjusted operating EPS—well within our target range of 40-60%, leaving ample room for reinvestment and resilience. This is supported by $4.2 billion in free cash flow from operations, up 12% year-over-year, driven by a P&C combined ratio of 94.2%—our best since 2019, excluding COVID outliers—and a book yield on our $85 billion fixed income portfolio of 4.1%, benefiting from the Fed’s rate hike cycle. Adjusted ROE came in at 13.4%, above our 12% hurdle rate, providing strong dividend coverage of 1.9x on a trailing twelve-month basis.

Regionally, this payout reflects divergent performances that underscore our diversification. In the U.S., which accounts for 62% of premiums, our personal lines auto segment saw earned premiums grow 8% amid hardening rates, +6.2% renewal pricing, offsetting $1.1 billion in cat losses from Hurricane Idalia and California wildfires. Commercial P&C here delivered a pristine 91.8% combined ratio, funding 55% of the annual dividend payout. Europe contributed solidly via our Lloyd’s syndicate and direct life operations, with embedded value growth of 7% in the UK and Germany, buoyed by IFRS 17 transition efficiencies that unlocked $450 million in capital release. Challenges in Asia-Pacific—particularly softer demand for accident & health products in Japan due to yen weakness—tempered growth to 3%, but our regional solvency ratio remains at 220%, well above local RBC equivalents.

From a technical standpoint, we’ve enhanced our dividend framework with several initiatives. First, our Dividend Reinvestment and Stock Purchase Plan, DRIP, saw 22% participation last year, with over 4 million shares reinvested at a 2% discount, accretive to EPS by 15 basis points. Second, we’re piloting an enhanced dividend overlay strategy using interest rate swaps to hedge duration risk on our portfolio, targeting a 50 basis points lift to net investment income in 2025. And while we repurchased $1.8 billion in shares at an average 18% discount to book value, we view dividends as the primary return vehicle—unlike Berkshire’s no-dividend model—balancing growth capex in telematics-enabled usage-based insurance and our digital platform, which drove 15% expense leverage.

Strategically, we’re committed to progressive dividend growth targeting 4-7% annually through the cycle, conditioned on maintaining a combined ratio under 96% and ROE above 12%. Inflationary pressures on loss costs—up 5.2% in body shop repairs and medical trends—are being met with 2025 rate actions averaging 5.8% across lines, plus AI-driven claims adjudication cutting cycle times by 28%. If cat activity moderates as modeled, 1-in-50 year return period, we see scope for a mid-single-digit hike at our next Board meeting. Geopolitically, we’ve stress-tested for $2 billion in cyber and supply chain risks, with reinsurance towers placed at 95% quota share above $500 million attachment via partners like Swiss Re and Munich Re.

In summary, our $2.72 per share dividend is not just sustainable—it’s a signal of our underwriting excellence and capital discipline in a hardening market. We’ll continue prioritizing total returns, with dividends at the core.

Finally, let's discuss a key component of our P&C underwriting results: reinsurance recoveries received and expected. This line item played a pivotal role in bolstering our combined ratio this quarter, coming in at 92.4%, down 180 basis points year-over-year.

Let me start with the headline numbers. In Q3, we recognized $478 million in reinsurance recoveries received, a 28% increase from the $373 million in Q3 2023. This reflects cash inflows from both prior-year development and current-period catastrophe events. Year-to-date through September 30th, cumulative recoveries received totaled $1.42 billion, up 22% from the prior-year period. These inflows directly supported our net loss and LAE reserves, reducing our statutory carried reserves by approximately 15% net of reinsurance.

Breaking it down by vintage, about 62% or $296 million of Q3 recoveries pertained to accident year 2024 losses, primarily driven by U.S. named storms—think Hurricane Idalia's landfall in Florida and the broader convective storm outbreaks across the Midwest. Our property catastrophe excess-of-loss, XoL, towers, placed with a diverse panel including Swiss Re, Munich Re, and Berkshire Hathaway Reinsurance Group, performed as expected, with recovery rates averaging 94% on ceded cat losses. This is a testament to the robust structures we renewed in our January 1st multi-year program, where we secured 95% retention of our prior capacity at mid-teens pricing—flat to down slightly despite the hardening market.

The remaining 38%, or $182 million, came from prior accident years. Notably, favorable development on 2022's Hurricane Ian recoveries added $112 million, with our quota-share treaties on Florida homeowners ceding 40% of net writings yielding an impressive 98% recovery realization rate. We've now fully collected under those layers, closing out what was a $2.1 billion gross cat event for us.

Now, turning to expected recoveries—this is where our forward-looking cedant strategy shines. As of quarter-end, we have $856 million in expected recoveries outstanding, up from $712 million at year-end 2023. Of this, $312 million is billable within the next 12 months, with the balance spread over 24-36 months under our proportional and XoL contracts. Our actuarial team, leveraging tools like RMS v18 models and our proprietary claims adjudication platform integrated with Guidewire ClaimCenter, has stress-tested these at a 95% confidence interval, factoring in reinsurer credit risk. We've allocated a modest $24 million adverse development cover, ADC, provision for potential disputes, primarily on European flood recoveries from Storm Babet earlier this year.

Regionally, the U.S. Southeast and Gulf Coast drove 55% of our Q3 inflows, reflecting our 35% market share in Florida homeowners via our Citizens depopulation program. Asia-Pacific contributed 22%, with typhoon recoveries from Saola and Haikui in Japan and the Philippines—our facultative placements with Korean Re and SCOR P&C there exceeded expectations at 91% recovery. Europe was softer at 14%, impacted by slower arbitration on German flood claims from 2021's Flood 21 event, but we're on track with Lloyd's syndicates for full settlement by Q1 2025. Emerging markets like LATAM rounded out the rest, with Chile earthquake residuals performing well under our regional excess programs.

On trends, we've seen a meaningful uptick in recovery velocity—average days-to-recover dropped 18% year-over-year to 142 days, thanks to our technical initiatives. We've rolled out AI-driven claims matching via our partnership with Duck Creek Technologies, which automates 75% of reinsurance billing notices, cutting leakage by 12%. Additionally, our shift toward parametric triggers in 15% of our 2024 cat placements—piloted with reinsurers like RenaissanceRe—has accelerated payouts by 60% for index-based events like California wildfires.

Strategically, this positions us well for 2025. With reinsurance pricing softening post-January renewals—down 5-10% in non-peak zones per Guy Carpenter's barometer—we're proactively optimizing our cession rates. We're targeting a 5-point increase in our gross net ratio through portfolio diversification, reducing U.S. cat exposure from 28% to 24% of net writings by layering in more industrial fire and cyber cat XoL from Hannover Re. This not only enhances recovery predictability but supports our ROE target of 14-16%.

Our reinsurance panel remains investment-grade heavy—98% A-rated or better—with no material disputes outstanding. We expect Q4 inflows of $220-250 million, keeping us on pace for $1.9 billion full-year recoveries, a 19% year-over-year increase.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the drivers behind your Personal Lines GWP growth, particularly in auto?

Mike Rivera: Good morning, David. Happy to elaborate. As Sarah detailed, Personal Auto grew 8.2%, with about 5.1% from rate increases averaging 6.8% via our GLMs and telematics from SafeDrive, which now has 4.2 million users. Volume added 3.1%, driven by 12% more new policies through digital channels. We're seeing strong demand there.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of recent market softening on your retention strategies?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, Lisa. Retention remains strong at 89.2% company-wide. Even with P&C rates softening 2.1% per indices, our pricing discipline holds renewals flat-to-up 3%. EagleEye AI predicts churn early, lifting retention 4.2%, and embedded partnerships secure 25% of renewals. We're guiding 90%+ for the year.

Operator: Our next question is from Robert Kline with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline: Thanks. On dividends, how sustainable is the 4-7% growth target amid potential cat volatility?

Sarah Thompson: Robert, our 48% payout ratio on adjusted EPS, 1.9x coverage, and $4.2 billion free cash flow provide a solid base. We're targeting that growth with combined ratio under 96% and ROE over 12%. Rate actions at 5.8% for 2025 offset loss cost inflation, and reinsurance buffers $2 billion in risks.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Maria Gonzalez: Good morning. Any updates on expected reinsurance recoveries for Q4?

Sarah Thompson: Yes, Maria. We expect $220-250 million in Q4 inflows, on track for $1.9 billion full-year, up 19%. Velocity is improving—142 days average—with AI automating 75% of billings. Our panel is 98% A-rated, and we're optimizing cessions for better gross net ratios.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] That concludes the question-and-answer session. I'll now turn the call back over to Mike Rivera for closing remarks.

Mike Rivera: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Global Assurance Holdings. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
